item.title: The heart-related blood test you may not have gotten — but should, according to medical experts
item.description: Lipoprotein(a) isn’t part of a standard lipid panel and is largely driven by genetics. Here’s why it’s important to get your level checked.

item.title: Maryland state park partially closed after rabid beavers attack visitors
item.description: A 13-year-old boy was attacked July 26 while swimming in the lake at Cunningham Falls State Park in Frederick County, according to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. More than a week later, another beaver bit a 19-year-old man fishing from the park’s shoreline on Wednesday.

item.title: This couple’s love of skating — and each other — outlived the mall rink where they met
item.description: Jerry and Tally Leonard have thrilled shoppers and open-skate crowds for decades at the Lloyd Center in Portland, Oregon. Now, they’re not sure how they will fill the void.

item.title: Jeanine Pirro, Trump’s longtime champion, is on the outs over Reflecting Pool move
item.description: D.C.’s top prosecutor spent a year navigating the president’s demands. Now she finds her job at risk amid a rare break with him over cases of alleged vandalism.

item.title: Rep. Max Miller has been battling for his career. Then came stories about a child’s stuffed bunny.
item.description: Many people seemed reluctant to take sides in the Ohio congressman’s bitter divorce until the allegation that he had withheld his young daughter’s sleep buddy.

item.title: Senate narrowly approves Blanche as AG, capping tough confirmation fight
item.description: The vote grants President Donald Trump’s former criminal defense lawyer a full stint as the head of the Justice Department, which has been rocked by vacancies and controversies.

item.title: One photo changed ‘Odyssey’ actress Samantha Morton’s life
item.description: The British actress’s understanding of art, and herself, was altered by an unexpected encounter with an intimately familiar image.

item.title: Avoiding these 3 risk factors might buy you 13 more dementia-free years
item.description: New research finds that people who steer clear of key cardiovascular hazards at midlife live much longer before developing dementia.

item.title: President Trump renews effort to fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook after Supreme Court ruling
item.description: The Supreme Court in June thwarted an earlier attempt by Trump to oust Cook, asserting the Federal Reserve's status as an independent agency.

item.title: Senate approves tough Russia sanctions bill after a year and a half of negotiations, a win for Ukraine supporters
item.description: The bill, which passed 86-11, now heads to the House, where lawmakers have already left Washington for the August recess. Supporters of the measure argue the bill could cripple the Kremlin’s main source of revenue and limit its ability to wage its war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year.

item.title: Trump says he’ll bring ballroom fight to Supreme Court after lower court halts work
item.description: An appeals court ruled earlier Friday that construction must stop until Congress authorizes the project. The ballroom is among the president’s top priorities for this term.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: His post-retirement hobby? ‘Improving’ his kids’ homes unasked.
item.description: Out-of-sorts workaholic scoffs at post-retirement advice — and instead starts projects at his grown kids’ homes without consent.

item.title: Sen. Bill Cassidy says he will back Todd Blanche for attorney general, appearing to clear way for confirmation
item.description: The Senate could hold the final vote on President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the Justice Department as soon as today.

item.title: Trump must halt aboveground ballroom construction, appeals court says
item.description: The order will take effect in two weeks, allowing the White House to appeal to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Freedom Fuel, praised by Trump, sells cheap gasoline. But how?
item.description: Despite recent price hikes, the mysterious company is still offering a significant discount at 29 stations across Pennsylvania and New Jersey.

item.title: Rep. Andy Ogles, a vocal Trump ally, loses Tennessee primary to Charlie Hatcher
item.description: Ogles had faced increased scrutiny over campaign finance decisions and other issues. Hatcher, a former state agriculture commissioner, received a boost this week with a late endorsement from Tennessee’s Republican governor, Bill Lee.

item.title: Sen. Marsha Blackburn, a longtime Trump ally, wins the GOP nomination for Tennessee governor
item.description: Blackburn’s victory capped a heated primary fight against Rep. John Rose. The Republican nominee will be favored to win the general election in the heavily red state.

item.title: New science overturns the conventional wisdom about brain games
item.description: Emerging evidence suggests that only certain types of training produce meaningful benefits, and those benefits may differ between men and women.

item.title: Trump tries new tack against birthright citizenship after Supreme Court snub, issuing orders certain to face legal challenges
item.description: The president signed executive orders that target children born to “alien enemies,” foreign lobbyists or tourists.

item.title: White House drafting executive order on vaccines and autism despite GOP pollsters’ warnings
item.description: The effort underscores President Donald Trump’s determination to elevate vaccine policy even as a judge has halted Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s sweeping vaccine overhaul and as voters are divided over the issue.

item.description: Prosecutors went after “ghost” school operators but rarely pursued student vets who enrolled just to collect housing subsidies, a Washington Post investigation finds.

item.title: Sen. Mitch McConnell says he has been discharged from a rehab center and will continue recovering at home after a fall in June
item.description: The Kentucky Republican, who has been away from the Senate for nearly two months, has not provided a timeline for his return to the Capitol.

item.title: Under Trump, 90% of ambassador nominations have gone to political supporters
item.description: More than any other president in recent history, Donald Trump is relying on wealthy donors and political loyalists rather than career diplomats to fill ambassadorships, a Washington Post analysis found.

item.title: How quickly can you prove that you’re a person? Try our quiz looking at the evolution of puzzles known as captchas.

item.description: Chairman Brendan Carr has long said he would do away with the ownership cap. Critics say only Congress has that authority.

item.description: I have serious questions about the Dominion-NextEra deal, and I intend to get answers.

item.title: Elon Musk’s DOGE made big errors in claims of government savings, government watchdog finds
item.description: The Government Accountability Office found that billions of dollars in DOGE’s public tally could not be verified and that some claimed cuts never happened.

Rand Paul (R-Kentucky), the committee’s chairman, has said that if the panel voted Thursday to hold Fauci in contempt, he would refer the matter directly to the Justice Department for potential prosecution.

item.title: Trump privately tells donors to back Vance while publicly keeping 2028 open
item.description: Advisers say the remark doesn’t mean the president has settled on a preferred candidate for 2028 as he plays up a contest between Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

item.description: Moderna said the new shot, which was approved after controversy and despite Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s skepticism, will probably be available at some retailers in the coming weeks.

item.title: U.S. moves to decertify transplant group that tried to collect organs from living patients
item.description: The investigation included the case of a Kentucky man who was brought to the operating table for organ recovery despite thrashing, crying and shaking his head.

item.title: Trump, Hegseth clashed at Camp David over shortages of long-range guided missiles and other critical munitions
item.description: While expressing frustration over the Iran war, the president demanded to know why he hadn't been notified that the weaponry was running drastically low, according to two people familiar with the conversation.

item.title: Michigan Senate primary shows Democratic establishment has lost its grip, columnist Karen Tumulty writes
item.description: The upset highlighted how out of touch the power brokers are with the party’s surging left wing as they try to retake control of the Senate.

item.title: Why ‘super movers’ have healthier brains — and how to be one
item.description: Defined as people who are able to walk significantly faster than most of their aging peers, they are about half as likely to experience cognitive decline, a study found.

item.title: Senate confirms CDC director after debate over whether she would defy RFK Jr.
item.description: Erica Schwartz, a physician and retired Navy rear admiral who served as deputy U.S. surgeon general during President Donald Trump’s first term, will take over as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s permanent director nearly a year after Trump fired Susan Monarez.

item.title: This federal judge ruled against Trump. Then the threats began.
item.description: U.S. District Judge John McConnell worked in relative obscurity for nearly all his 15 years on the federal bench. Starting early last year, he faced a wave of intimidation that was unlike anything he had ever experienced and that signaled a new era for federal judges.

item.title: Social media is fueling limerence, an intense form of romantic obsession
item.description: These episodes of profound infatuation — characterized by frequent thoughts about a love interest, moods dependent on their actions and vivid fantasy — have appeared in art and literature throughout history. But the digital world is primed to feed them.

item.title: How Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s contentious Senate Democratic primary
item.description: When the left-wing candidate entered the race in 2025, he was an underdog who was best known for losing the 2018 primary for governor to Gretchen Whitmer by 22 points. He overcame a massive spending disadvantage and opposition from party leaders to win Tuesday’s primary on a message of drastically changing the political system.

item.title: Temporary protected status for Haitians officially ends, putting thousands out of work and in limbo
item.description: A federal judge on Wednesday took the final step in allowing the Trump administration to terminate temporary protected status for 350,000 Haitians, meaning many are likely to lose their jobs and be at risk of deportation back to a country the United States says remains dangerous.
